text: The question is on the lips of every scribe by the door. Do you ask it too?
The question is on the lips of every scribe by the door. Do you whisper it too?
You say nothing. The others say it for you, loud enough for the room to hear.
A toll collector, of all people. What do you think?
You came to Capernaum as one of the healthy. You are still standing by the door.
When the teaching ends, he does not go back toward the town. He walks along the shore, straight toward the toll booth.
You say it with them, to one of his disciples, loud enough for the room to hear.
He leaves the coins where they lie. The merchant stares at the empty booth, then at the money, and does not touch it.
The toll collector does not look up from his counting. No one stands near his booth who does not have to.
Toll on the way out of Philip’s land, toll on the way into this one. By the time I reach Tiberias, I’ll have paid for the cloth twice.

Capernaum lay near the border between Herod Antipas’s Galilee and Philip’s territory. Goods crossing it paid tolls, collected by local men who bought the right. Most people despised them as cheats who served foreign rulers.
You and the other scribes stand just inside the door. None of you sits down.
You were at the house yesterday? Then you know why we watch him. A teacher is known by the company he keeps. Watch where he goes.
You stand just inside the door with the women of Levi’s household, who are carrying in the dishes. The scribes stand by the door too. None of them sits down.
He went out again by the seaside. All the multitude came to him, and he taught them.
As he passed by, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office, and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he arose and followed him.
It happened, that he was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.
When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
The scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”
